dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. Good morning.
Good morning, Denise. My name is Yuki Singh. I'm calling about the water out front of my house. It's the storm drain, and I'm, well, I'm pretty fed up, to be honest with you.
Okay, Ms. Singh, tell me what's going on. What's the address?
281 Bellevue Avenue. Up in the Bellevue section. Right about across from the stone wall there.
Got it. And the drain out front, is it backed up?

Backed up, yes. Since the storm. That snow-to-rain business, Sunday into Monday. All that snow melted and the rain came on top of it and the drain just sat there full. It's still a puddle out there, a big one, almost across the whole width of the road edge, and it's Tuesday now.
Yeah, that was a lot of snowmelt at once. Is the water in the street only, or has it gotten onto your property?

Well, that's the thing. It came in the cellar. A few inches. Seeped right in along the wall. I've lived in this house a long, long time, and that has never happened. Never. Not once. And I told myself, somebody ought to be clearing those drains before the weather turns, wicked obvious, no?
I hear you. A few inches in the cellar, that's no small thing. Is the water still coming in, or has it stopped?

It's stopped coming in. It's just sitting there now. I got the wet vac going yesterday, and I got most of it, but the drain out front is what I'm worried about, because if it rains again it's going to do the same thing.
Right. Let me get this down. Two eighty-one Bellevue, storm drain at the curb in front is clogged or backed up, water into the cellar. Do you see leaves, ice, any debris sitting on the grate?
Leaves, and a lot of ice chunks, kind of packed in there. Gray slush. You can't even see the grate really. Somebody's plow probably shoved it all over it.
That's very possible. Okay, and is the water in the road deep enough that a car would have trouble?

Cars slow down and go around, they splash right up. But what's got me is the walkers. We get kids walking home, and the dog walkers, people up and down here all day. The water's right at the edge, and with the cold it skims over with ice at night. Somebody's going to step in it or slip, and a little one could really get hurt.
That's a fair concern. I'm going to mark this as a priority because of the foot traffic and the water getting into your house. I'll send it to the crew that handles catch basins.
Thank you. Because I called, well, I haven't called before. But I've been looking at it since yesterday morning and nobody has come by. Nobody. Not even to put a cone out.
Yeah, they've had a long list since the storm ended. I can't tell you the hour, but it'll go to the top of today's requests, and I'd expect somebody out there today or tomorrow.
Today or tomorrow. Okay. I'm going to hold you to that, Denise, nicely.
That's fair. Can I get a number to reach you?
Sure. It's 401-555-0170. That's the house phone, so if I'm out, just let it ring a while, or leave a message. I might be at the bank.
Okay, 401-555-0170. Anything I should know about getting to the drain? A car parked there, a gate, anything like that?

No, nothing. It's right at the curb, front of the hedge. My car's in the driveway. Oh, and I do have to go to the bank later, I need a notary stamp on a form, so if the crew comes while I'm gone, that's fine, they don't need me.
Good, that makes it easy. They'll just do the work at the curb. Now, once it's cleared, do you want a call back?
Yes, please. When it's done, give me a ring. I'd like to know it's actually been done and not just written down on a piece of paper somewhere.
I'll put a note on the request to call you when it's closed out. You have it as the house line, right?
That's the one. The landline. It's old but it works.

Those are the best kind. Now, in the meantime, if the water in your cellar gets any higher or it starts raining hard again, call us back right away. And if the puddle out front freezes over, maybe keep an eye on it for those walkers.
I'll put a couple of orange cones out there if I can find them. My late, no, never mind. I've got a couple in the garage somewhere.
That would help. Just stay on your side of the curb when you set them out, with the cars going by.
Yes, yes, I will. I'm not going to go out in the road, I'm too old for that.
Good. Okay, Ms. Singh, you're all set on my end. Request is in, flagged for the crew, and we'll call you when it's done.
Thank you, Denise. I appreciate you taking it seriously. I'm still not happy about the cellar, but that's not on you.
I understand. Hang in there, and take care of yourself.
You too. Bye now.
